# OC for the hollow double triangle with equal vertex-fiber volumes

This is a proved family consequence of the three-quarter source
bound. It does not resolve arbitrary vertex volumes or general OC.

## Theorem

Let d>=1 and let C be a convex body in R^2 x R^d whose integer
projection is

    P=conv{v_0=(0,0),v_1=(2,0),v_2=(0,2)}.

Assume its three vertex fibers K_i=C_(v_i) have the same positive
d-volume a. No equality, shape, centroid, or regularity assumption is
made on these bodies or on the three midpoint fibers

    B_ij=C_((v_i+v_j)/2), b_ij=|B_ij|, 0<=i<j<=2.

Then a single actual mixed-integer point y belongs to a midpoint
fiber and satisfies, for EVERY closed ambient halfspace H containing y,

    H_d(C intersect (Z^2 x R^d) intersect H)
       >=(gamma_d/4) H_d(C intersect (Z^2 x R^d)).       (1)

The projection P has exactly six integer points, namely the three
vertices and their three edge midpoints. All six fibers have positive
d-volume, as proved below, so intrinsic q=d and the measure in (1)
is exactly the ordinary sum of their d-volumes. The conclusion includes
oblique halfspaces and halfspaces containing an entire fiber.

## Proof

For each edge, convexity gives

    (K_i+K_j)/2 subset B_ij.

Brunn-Minkowski therefore implies b_ij>=a. Let b be the largest of
the three numbers b_ij, and choose an edge attaining it. Relabel its
two endpoint bodies A and E and its midpoint body B. The total mixed
volume is

    M=3a+b_01+b_02+b_12<=3(a+b).                      (2)

There exists a finite coupling of uniform volumes on A and E, each
of mass a, whose midpoint pushforward eta is dominated by ordinary
volume on B. For clarity, this density fact has the following direct
proof. Normalize endpoint densities to probability densities bounded
by 1/a, smooth them by a Gaussian, and use increasing triangular
transport T between the smoothed laws. The midpoint map (Id+T)/2
has determinant at least sqrt(det DT). Its density is consequently
at most the geometric mean of the two endpoint densities, hence at
most 1/a. A tight weak limit retains the original marginals and this
density bound. Multiplying by a yields eta<=dx; its support lies in
(A+E)/2 subset B. Thus eta(B)=a and eta<=1_B dx.

Let x be the centroid of rho=1_B dx+2eta, and let m be the chosen
integer midpoint. This is a deterministic choice from an attained
coupling, and x belongs to B by convexity. Set y=(m,x), which lies
in S itself.

Fix a closed ambient halfspace H containing y. If an average of the
two lifted source points lies in H, at least one source point lies
in H, since an affine defining functional preserves their average.
Integrating this indicator implication against the coupling gives

    eta(H_m)<=|A intersect H_(v_i)|+|E intersect H_(v_j)|.

All other original fibers contribute nonnegative mass. Consequently

    H_d(S intersect H)>=|B intersect H_m|+eta(H_m).    (3)

When H has a nonzero continuous normal, H_m is a closed continuous
halfspace containing x. The proved three-quarter bound in
`candidate 6b83c9ea944bc6c0` gives

    |B intersect H_m|+eta(H_m)>=(3 gamma_d/4)(b+a).

When the continuous normal vanishes, H_m is all of R^d because it
contains x, and the same inequality follows from b+a>0 and
3 gamma_d/4<=1. Thus this step covers every orientation and all
closed-boundary cases. Combining it with (2)-(3) proves (1).

Only ordinary Brunn-Minkowski, the proved dominated midpoint coupling,
and the proved three-quarter inequality enter this argument. It does
not replace a sum of integer fibers by a projection integral or move
the selected point away from the integer midpoint.

## Scope

The middle fibers may have arbitrary unequal volumes and arbitrary
convex shapes. The three endpoint fibers may also have arbitrary
shapes, provided their volumes are equal and positive. The body need
not be polyhedral or symmetric. The projection is hollow of lattice
width two, so this family is distinct from width-one splits.

The positive-volume hypothesis at the three vertices is explicit.
Neither lower-dimensional vertex fibers nor unequal positive vertex
volumes are covered by this theorem. Its fixed two-dimensional integer
projection is an additional assumption, so it is not the task's full
arbitrary-n,d conclusion.
